about: Known-answer cases for sg:annual-report-after-extension-limit:v1, each worked by hand and by a separate script, with no person in them. A case names what the Signal must do, and why, in the rule's own terms.
rule: Due 15 May of the year after the filing year, moved to the next business day where it falls on a weekend or a federal holiday. The latest date is the later of 15 May + 90 days and the due date + 90 days, moved to the next business day where it falls on one. Fires where the report is dated two days or more after the latest date (5 U.S.C. § 13103(d), (g)(1); the Committee's 2025 Instruction Guide).

cases.name: dated on the due date
cases.why: 15 May 2026 is a Friday, so the due date does not move. A report dated on it is not after it.

cases.name: the day after the due date
cases.why: Inside the 90 days an extension may add. The register does not decide whether one covered it, so it is not evaluated, whatever extension the register holds or does not.

expect.reason: after its due date, within the time an extension may cover

cases.name: the ninetieth day
cases.why: 15 May 2026 + 90 days is Thursday 13 August 2026, the latest date any extension could reach. A report dated on it may be covered by an extension.

expect.reason: after its due date, within the time an extension may cover

cases.name: the day after the latest date
cases.why: Not evaluated: a report submitted late in the evening of 13 August could carry the next day's date, and the register has not established the filing system's clock.

expect.reason: the day after the latest date, whose clock the register has not established

cases.name: two days after the latest date
cases.why: Fires: no extension the statute allows outside a combat zone reaches 15 August 2026. 2 days after 13 August; 92 after 15 May (16 to 31 May, 30, 31, 15).

expect.description: This is an annual financial disclosure report for calendar year 2025. The Clerk's index dates it 2026-08-15, the same date the report prints as its filing date and its signature line gives. It was due 2026-05-15. The statute lets extensions add at most 90 days (5 U.S.C. § 13103(d), (g)(1)), so the latest date any extension could reach was 2026-08-13. The report is dated 2 days after that date and 92 days after its due date. The register cannot see an extension for service in a combat zone, which 5 U.S.C. § 13103(g)(2) allows beyond 90 days.

cases.name: well after the latest date, with no extension anywhere
cases.why: Fires the same way whether or not any extension row exists, because none could reach this date: 38 days after 13 August (18 + 20), 128 after 15 May.

cases.name: a due date on a Saturday, as in 2027
cases.why: Filing year 2026: 15 May 2027 is a Saturday, so the report is due Monday 17 May 2027. A report dated that Monday is not after its due date.

cases.name: the latest date, the later reading, off the weekend
cases.why: 15 May 2027 + 90 is Friday 13 August; 17 May + 90 is Sunday 15 August. The later reading, moved off the weekend, is Monday 16 August 2027, so 17 August is the day after and not evaluated.

expect.reason: the day after the latest date, whose clock the register has not established

cases.name: two days after the later reading
cases.why: Fires: 2 days after Monday 16 August 2027; 93 days after Monday 17 May 2027 (14 + 30 + 31 + 18).

expect.description: This is an annual financial disclosure report for calendar year 2026. The Clerk's index dates it 2027-08-18, the same date the report prints as its filing date and its signature line gives. It was due 2027-05-17, the first business day after 2027-05-15, a Saturday. The statute lets extensions add at most 90 days (5 U.S.C. § 13103(d), (g)(1)), so the latest date any extension could reach was 2027-08-16, the first business day after 2027-08-15, a Sunday. The report is dated 2 days after that date and 93 days after its due date. The register cannot see an extension for service in a combat zone, which 5 U.S.C. § 13103(g)(2) allows beyond 90 days.

cases.name: dates that disagree
cases.why: The index gives 20 September and the report prints 19 September. Not evaluated: which one is the filing date is not the register's to choose.

expect.reason: the index date, the printed filing date and the signature date disagree

cases.name: no filing year printed
cases.why: A header with no Filing Year line: the due date cannot be known from the document.

cases.name: a year whose instructions were not read
cases.why: Filing year 2024: the register has read the Committee's instructions for 2025 only.

expect.reason: a filing year whose instructions the register has not read

cases.name: sixty-one days of service
cases.why: Sworn in 1 November 2025: 1 November to 31 December is 61 days, more than 60, so the report is required and evaluated.

cases.name: sixty days of service
cases.why: Sworn in 2 November 2025: 60 days, not more than 60, so the rule may not require the report. Not evaluated.

expect.reason: 60 days or fewer of service in the filing year, by the swearing-in recorded

cases.name: no swearing-in recorded
cases.why: The roster records no swearing-in, so the service condition cannot be read.

cases.name: an amendment is not an annual report
cases.why: Its header says Amendment Report, whatever its code. The Signal does not read it at all.

cases.name: a paper report, whose header the register cannot read
cases.why: No printed fields: the Signal cannot know from the document that it is annual, and reads no code, so it is not among the reports it evaluates.

cases.name: a candidate's report
cases.why: Status: Congressional Candidate. The Signal reads Members' reports.
